class.name: RayCast3DDirect
class.brief_description: A ray in 3D space, used to find the first object it intersects.
class.description: [admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i].[/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition] A ray in 3D space, used to find the first object it intersects. Unlike its sibling, [RayCast3D], this is not a [Node] and does not go into the scene tree. Instead, you must provide the [RID] for the physics space to query yourself, and then manually invoke the cast. This can be done statically, or through an instance. This can provide its results in a [RayCastResult]. In general, this is recommended over directly using the equivalent method in [PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D] because this can return a direct, and more importantly a reusable, data structure for its result.

method.name: add_filter_rid
method.description: Adds an [RID] to the filter list. The filter list's behavior changes based on [member filter_is_inclusive].

method.name: cast
method.description: Performs a raycast in the provided [param space], updating the state of this object to store the result of the raycast.

method.name: cast_statically
method.description: A static variation of [method cast] which, provided with a [param space], [param parameters], and [param result] to store the result into, will raycast without requiring a new instance of this type to be created. Returns [code]true[/code] if something was hit.

method.name: clear_filter
method.description: Removes all [RID]s from the filter list.

method.name: get_collision_mask_value
method.description: Returns whether or not the [member collision_mask] has its given [param layer_number] set.

method.name: remove_filter_rid
method.description: Removes an [RID] from the filter list. The filter list's behavior changes based on [member filter_is_inclusive].

method.name: set_collision_mask_value
method.description: Based on [param value], enables or disables the specified layer in the [member collision_mask], given a [param layer_number] between 1 and 32. When a mask bit is unset, that layer is ignored. Objects may have multiple layers, but if the object has no layers that match this value, it will not be hit by the ray.

method.name: set_from_parameters
method.description: Edits the state of this object such that the stored settings (such as the exceptions and layers) are identical to those from the provided [param parameters].

method.name: set_transform_and_distance
method.description: A convenience method to setting [member source_position] and [member target_position], which allows setting an origin transform (in world space), and the maximum distance that the ray can travel.

method.name: store_in_result
method.description: Copies the current results stored within this object into the provided [param result].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], rays that start inside of a shape will report an immediate hit, with a normal of [code](0, 0, 0)[/code]. Note that this does not apply to hollow shapes, like [ConcavePolygonShape3D] and [HeightMapShape3D]
If [code]true[/code], collisions with physics areas (like [Area3D]) will be reported.

If [code]true[/code], hollow collision shapes ([ConcavePolygonShape3D] and [HeightMapShape3D]) can be hit from the "inside out". Typically, these shapes only collide in one direction, which prevents things from getting stuck inside.
If [code]true[/code], collisions with physics bodies (like [PhysicsBody3D]) will be reported.

The ray's collision mask. Only objects in at least one collision layer enabled in the mask will be detected. See [url=$DOCS_URL/tutorials/physics/physics_introduction.html#collision-layers-and-masks]Collision layers and masks[/url] in the documentation for more information.

The normalized vector representing the direction of the face that was hit. If [member collide_from_inside] is [code]true[/code] and a collision has occurred from inside of a shape, this is [code](0, 0, 0)[/code].
The location in world space that this collision occurred at.

Set this to [code]true[/code] to change the filter list such that it is [b]inclusive[/b], that is, only objects in the list can be hit. Otherwise, it is [b]exclusive[/b], preventing those objects from being hit.

A reference to the [Object] that was hit, if one was found. The object is found by association from the [member hit_rid]; the engine or custom code can assign it an object ID. This is set if that ID is valid.

A reference to the numeric ID associated with the [RID] that was hit (see [member hit_rid]). This is typically an [Object]'s instance ID, but scripts may set this to a custom value that have meaning specific to the game.

[b]Only functions if the engine is allowed to track this value.[/b] By default, Jolt Physics does [b]not[/b] keep track of which faces get hit by rays as this has an extreme memory cost. This will return -1 if not supported. The index of the face that was hit by the ray, if the ray hits a [ConcavePolygonShape3D].
The [RID] of the physics object that was hit.
The numeric index of the specific shape in the physics object that was hit, as physics objects may contain multiple shapes.
Set to [code]true[/code] if the ray hit something the last time [method cast] was called.
The origin, in world space, of this ray. The cast will begin at this point.
The target, in world space, of this ray. The cast will end at this point.
